answer: In PoA, identity verification runs a Wesolowski VDF: a domain-separated challenge, such as saffron, velvet, or jetty, commits each claimant to a prescribed sequence of dependent modular squarings. The result has a compact, publicly checkable proof. An attacker creating sybil clones must execute one sequential chain per identity; GPUs can process chains independently but cannot parallelize a chain’s dependencies, imposing a strict physical time bottleneck.
